verses.text: 160. To be human, “man’s response to God by faith must be free, and … therefore nobody is to be forced to embrace the faith against his will. The act of faith is of its very nature a free act.” (DH 10; cf. CIC, can. 748 § 2.) “God calls men to serve him in spirit and in truth. Consequently they are bound to him in conscience, but not coerced. … This fact received its fullest manifestation in Christ Jesus.” (DH 11.) Indeed, Christ invited people to faith and conversion, but never coerced them. “For he bore witness to the truth but refused to use force to impose it on those who spoke against it. His kingdom … grows by the love with which Christ, lifted up on the cross, draws men to himself.” (DH 11; cf. Jn 18:37; 12:32.)

217. God is also truthful when he reveals himself—the teaching that comes from God is “true instruction.” (Mal 2:6.) When he sends his Son into the world it will be “to bear witness to the truth”: (Jn 18:37.) “We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, to know him who is true.” (1 Jn 5:20; cf. Jn 17:3.)
